description: The description field is the only part of the skill in context on every turn. Six prompts that should fire it — including the two the description calls out without the words 'threat model' (pentest scope, a new AI agent feature) — and six adjacent security or engineering prompts it must not hijack: dependency audits, a code review for one bug class, a conceptual question, a secret rotation, and ordinary feature work.

probes.prompt: Before we ship the inbound email webhook to customers, what could go wrong security-wise? Write it down for the team.
We have an external pentest booked for next week. What should we tell them to focus on in this API?
Draw a data flow diagram of this service with the trust boundaries marked.
We're adding an agent that reads the inbound support emails and can refund customers through Stripe. Anything we should worry about before building it?
Do a STRIDE pass over the ticket endpoints.
Our security hackathon is Friday — put together the scope of what the teams should try to break here.
Run npm audit and bump whatever is vulnerable.
Explain how SameSite cookies protect against CSRF.
I think a Stripe key leaked in a commit last week. How do I rotate it?
Write unit tests for priorityScore in src/routes/tickets.ts.
Add a GET /tickets endpoint that lists the 20 most recent tickets.
